Formula: respondent x basket pairs where observed Ownly saving >= that respondent's stated required recurring saving / all such pairs
Interpretation: Falls 81% -> 56% -> 27% across the three price views. This is the study's central number: it answers 'is the saving big enough for these people' rather than 'is Ownly cheaper'.
Caveat: Cross-product of a stated threshold and an observed price; n=4 baskets. Not a conversion rate.

Formula: baskets Ownly wins on list+fees but loses after incumbent coupons / matched baskets
Interpretation: Measures how much of the structural advantage a coupon can erase on any given day.
Caveat: n=4. Ownly held a new-account intro offer; incumbents held memberships.

Formula: baskets Ownly wins on list+fees but loses once the incumbent MEMBERSHIP benefit alone applies, before any coupon / matched baskets
Interpretation: Isolates the DURABLE half of the erosion. A membership is a standing benefit applying to every order; a coupon is episodic. Ownly can out-wait a coupon, not a subscription — and 82% of this catchment holds one.

Basis: Sheet 1 — Unit Market Share / Volume Share
Formula: Ownly orders in last 4 weeks / all delivery orders in last 4 weeks, WITHIN THE SAMPLE. Respondents whose Ownly count contradicts their own other answers are excluded from the numerator, not counted as zero — so the catchment figure is a LOWER BOUND.
Interpretation: In this catchment sample Swiggy takes 54.6% and Zomato 36.8% of reported orders. Ownly's usable count is 0 orders, with 1 response unusable, so its share is a lower bound rather than a measured zero. Bengaluru — live far longer — shows 2.05%, which is what early traction looks like when it exists.
Caveat: THIS IS NOT MARKET SHARE. It is share of orders inside a small convenience sample. The formula-sheet Volume Share needs total market unit sales, which this study does not have. Ownly has been live in Hyderabad for weeks, so a low share here is expected and is NOT evidence of rejection.

Formula: Brand Penetration (%) / Market Penetration (%) = Ownly triers / category orderers
Interpretation: Of the people in this sample who order food delivery at all, 5.6% have ever tried Ownly. The formula-sheet version uses total population as the denominator; here the denominator is the sample, so it is a within-sample penetration share.
Caveat: Sample, not population. 'Ever tried' not 'active user'. Very low base.

Formula: Ownly orders / total category orders BY OWNLY USERS
Interpretation: Among people who actually use Ownly, what share of their delivery ordering it captures. This is the closest available proxy for the frequency half of the North Star.
Caveat: n=2 users across all cities. Directional only; cannot be reported by city.

Formula: respondents paying the ₹30 premium to keep most usual restaurants / respondents shown the item
Interpretation: [95% CI 50-78%] The highest refusal of the three ₹30 trades — the one thing money could not buy in this sample.

Formula: Rapido users who have NOT noticed food in the app / Rapido users
Interpretation: [95% CI 69-93%] Distribution exists; discovery largely does not.

Formula: (% top-2 likely to TRY) - (% top-2 likely to CONTINUE after the intro offer ends)
Interpretation: Trial intent 78% vs post-offer continuation 25%. The size of the drop is the rented-demand risk expressed in this sample's own words.
Caveat: STATED INTENT PROXY. The two items use different framings, so part of the gap is framing.

Formula: median incumbent non-food share of bill - median Ownly non-food share
Interpretation: Expresses Ownly's structural edge as the share of the bill that is not food. It survives without subsidy, unlike a discount — and it is invisible to the customer unless stated, which ties the metric to the communication problem.
Caveat: Median across priced captures; excludes menu-price differences.
